packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-03 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (isolated first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of this item. This is a blind reading. I have not tried to identify work or author.

Conventions: (..) = my expansion of an abbreviation; ? after a word = uncertain reading; [illegible] = unreadable; [..] = lost/damaged. In this hand "e" is regularly written like "o"/"v", "est" is a single small stroke (rendered e(st)), "esse" is "ee"/"ve" (rendered esse), "non" a single "o"/"n" stroke (rendered n(on)); I have normalised those letter-forms silently but kept abbreviations marked. Line numbers are counted from the top of each named tile and are approximate where a tile begins mid-line.

=====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
=====================================================================
Three views:
- image-001 (overview): a single small upright leaf, ca. 9 x 13 cm by the ruler, single column, ca. 33 lines, long lines, very small rapid cursive in brown ink. Heavy staining upper right, a library stamp lower right ("BIBL. UNIV / GEN[..]"). At the very top edge an underlined line of writing shows from a leaf lying underneath, and in the upper-right damaged area words of the underlying leaf show through a loss; so the top 3-4 lines of this view mix two leaves. Tiles 002-007 belong to this view.
- image-008 (overview): an opened bifolium, ca. 23 cm wide; left page irregularly torn at top-left and left edge, right page nearly complete. Single column each page. Tiles 009-014 belong to this view. The right-hand page of this opening is the leaf whose top line showed beneath the small leaf in image-001.
- image-015 (overview): another opening of the same booklet (sewing holes visible in the gutter), single column each page. Tiles 016-021 belong to this view.
Observed features: no running titles, no rubrication, no enlarged or decorated initials. Short entries are separated by horizontal pen rules drawn across the column. Several entries are preceded by a centred heading line in the same hand and ink (question titles). One centred word "Finis" with a flourish, followed by a ruled line and a new centred heading. Interlinear corrections and struck-through words occur; one whole four-line entry is struck through (image-018). No marginal glosses seen. Tentative interpretation (not observation): a student's or teacher's notebook of short question-and-answer notes (heading, "R(espond)eo", "probatur", "Dices", "Dico"), not a main text with commentary.

Areas selected: I read every tile; the spans below cover nearly all the writing. Areas left unread or only partly read are listed in section 5.
